## Xi Jinping in 2024: `2B.1` diplomacy vs force-first

Best read: **mixed, but with more evidence of de-escalatory rhetoric than of actual compromise.** Xi/China repeatedly used diplomatic and peace language in 2024, especially on Ukraine and nuclear risk. But the clearest operational evidence around Taiwan still points to coercive force signaling, not clear preference for peaceful alternatives.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Supports diplomacy | [Wang Yi Elaborates on China's Position on Ukraine Crisis](https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/xw/zyxw/202405/t20240530_11332760.html) | PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs | 2024-02-18 | https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/xw/zyxw/202405/t20240530_11332760.html | Wang Yi attributed to Xi a line favoring nuclear restraint and a peaceful settlement of the Ukraine crisis, including protecting nuclear materials and facilities. That is not a full diplomacy test, but it is consistent with de-escalation when peaceful alternatives exist. | `2B.1`, `1B.1`, `1B.2`, `1B.4` |

This is direct de-escalatory evidence, but still doctrinal rather than a concrete compromise. | `2B.1`, `1B.4`, `1B.8` |

That is force-first signaling in a live flashpoint, not evidence of choosing compromise over coercion. | `2B.1`, `6A`, `1B.8` |

| Cuts against `2B.1` | [Senior Defense Official Briefs on 2024 China Military Power Report](https://www.defense.gov/News/Transcripts/Transcript/Article/4009708/senior-defense-official-briefs-on-2024-china-military-power-report/) | U.S. Department of Defense | 2024-12-18 | https://www.defense.gov/News/Transcripts/Transcript/Article/4009708/senior-defense-official-briefs-on-2024-china-military-power-report/ | DoD said China surpassed 600 operational nuclear warheads by mid-2024 and kept expanding rapidly. That points to coercive leverage and modernization, not a clean preference for diplomacy. | `2B.1`, `1B.1` |

### Synthesis

- **Best evidence for `2B.1`:** Xi’s 2024 public line consistently favored diplomacy, peaceful coexistence, nuclear restraint, and arms-control language.
- **Best evidence against `2B.1`:** The Taiwan drills and rapid nuclear buildup show force and coercion remained central tools.
- **Bottom line:** **partial support only.** I found strong de-escalatory rhetoric, but not strong proof that Xi chose compromise over force when a credible peaceful alternative was on the table.

### Search gap

I did **not** find a 2024 case where Xi personally made a concrete compromise in a crisis and clearly rejected a force-based option that was still available. The record is mostly **rhetorical de-escalation plus coercive military practice**.
